answer: Expiring compute-trace pricing requires each identity to submit a signed compute trace per epoch, with length scaled by a public beacon so the per-identity verification fee rises as new identities outrun verified compute hours. Prepaid fees sit in a vault and decay unused, so an attacker cannot recycle one pool across clones. A walnut-sized honest device clears one trace cheaply, while 10,000 sybils need 10,000 concurrent runtimes and pay the rising fee per epoch.
